# Charts

A chart is the table of its numbers, drawn: columns stacked by day, a sparkline of the last runs, a board of lanes over the next hours. The numbers stay in the page as text, so a screen reader reads the table; a small script only hands them to the stylesheet.

## A package of the release

Charts are linked apart, on the screens that show them, beside the two files: `css/redz-ui-charts.min.css` draws, and `js/redz-ui-charts.min.js` hands it the numbers - every `data-v`, `data-at`, `data-from`, `data-to`, `data-median` and `data-now` becomes a custom property through the CSSOM, which a strict CSP allows where it would refuse a `style` attribute. A number is a share, 0 to 1: a value over the largest, a time over the window.

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="redz-ui/css/redz-ui-charts.min.css">
<script type="module" src="redz-ui/js/redz-ui-charts.min.js"></script>
```

## Columns by day

`table class="chart"`: its `caption` is the title, the header cells after the first are the series and draw as the legend, and each row is a day - `th scope="row"` its label, each `td` a segment whose `data-v` is its share of the tallest day, stacked from the first up. The series take eight colors in order, `--redz-chart-1` to `-8`, chosen to stay apart for color-blind eyes in both themes; `data-tone` gives a segment a state's color instead. A row's `title` is its tooltip, a row with `data-empty` a stub on the axis, and a label wrapped in `visually-hidden` is read, not shown - label every few days when there are many. `--redz-chart-height` sets the height, 10rem by default; ninety days fit a card 700 px wide.

```html
<table class="chart">
	<caption>Messages sent per day</caption>
	<thead><tr><th scope="col">Day</th><th scope="col" data-tone="success">Free</th><th scope="col" data-tone="warning">Paid</th><th scope="col" data-tone="danger">Failed</th></tr></thead>
	<tbody>
		<tr title="Nov 1: 120 free, 30 paid, 4 failed"><th scope="row">Nov 1</th><td data-tone="success" data-v="0.615">120</td><td data-tone="warning" data-v="0.154">30</td><td data-tone="danger" data-v="0.021">4</td></tr>
		<tr title="Nov 2: 132 free, 28 paid, 2 failed"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 2</span></th><td data-tone="success" data-v="0.677">132</td><td data-tone="warning" data-v="0.144">28</td><td data-tone="danger" data-v="0.01">2</td></tr>
		<tr title="Nov 3: 98 free, 41 paid, 6 failed"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 3</span></th><td data-tone="success" data-v="0.503">98</td><td data-tone="warning" data-v="0.21">41</td><td data-tone="danger" data-v="0.031">6</td></tr>
		<tr data-empty title="Nov 4: none"><th scope="row">Nov 4</th><td>0</td><td>0</td><td>0</td></tr>
		<tr title="Nov 5: 144 free, 35 paid, 3 failed"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 5</span></th><td data-tone="success" data-v="0.738">144</td><td data-tone="warning" data-v="0.179">35</td><td data-tone="danger" data-v="0.015">3</td></tr>
		<tr title="Nov 6: 160 free, 22 paid, 1 failed"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 6</span></th><td data-tone="success" data-v="0.821">160</td><td data-tone="warning" data-v="0.113">22</td><td data-tone="danger" data-v="0.005">1</td></tr>
		<tr title="Nov 7: 110 free, 30 paid, 9 failed"><th scope="row">Nov 7</th><td data-tone="success" data-v="0.564">110</td><td data-tone="warning" data-v="0.154">30</td><td data-tone="danger" data-v="0.046">9</td></tr>
```

`chart-values` writes each column's number above it - for one series and a few columns, where the numbers are what a person reads.

```html
<table class="chart chart-values">
	<caption>Guests per month</caption>
	<thead><tr><th scope="col">Month</th><th scope="col">Guests</th></tr></thead>
	<tbody>
		<tr><th scope="row">Jul</th><td data-v="0.55">220</td></tr>
		<tr><th scope="row">Aug</th><td data-v="0.7">280</td></tr>
		<tr><th scope="row">Sep</th><td data-v="0.45">180</td></tr>
		<tr><th scope="row">Oct</th><td data-v="0.6">240</td></tr>
		<tr><th scope="row">Nov</th><td data-v="0.85">340</td></tr>
		<tr><th scope="row">Dec</th><td data-v="1">400</td></tr>
	</tbody>
</table>
```

### A line

`chart chart-line` draws one series as a line with its area under it, through each row's first `data-v`: the script draws one SVG behind the rows, so the line is one stroke at any width, and each row keeps its tooltip and marks its point under the pointer. The scale is the page's: `data-v` is a share of the range it chose - from the lowest to the highest day, padded - and the captions say it. The header names the series for a screen reader and is hidden from sight.

```html
<table class="chart chart-line" data-tooltips>
	<caption>Storage used, last 14 days</caption>
	<thead><tr><th scope="col">Day</th><th scope="col">Used</th></tr></thead>
	<tbody><tr title="Nov 1 · 40.5 GB"><th scope="row">Nov 1</th><td data-v="0.42">40.5 GB</td></tr><tr title="Nov 2 · 41.2 GB"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 2</span></th><td data-v="0.45">41.2 GB</td></tr><tr title="Nov 3 · 41.0 GB"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 3</span></th><td data-v="0.44">41.0 GB</td></tr><tr title="Nov 4 · 42.5 GB"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 4</span></th><td data-v="0.5">42.5 GB</td></tr><tr title="Nov 5 · 42.0 GB"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 5</span></th><td data-v="0.48">42.0 GB</td></tr><tr title="Nov 6 · 43.8 GB"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 6</span></th><td data-v="0.55">43.8 GB</td></tr><tr title="Nov 7 · 44.5 GB"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 7</span></th><td data-v="0.58">44.5 GB</td></tr><tr title="Nov 8 · 44.2 GB"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 8</span></th><td data-v="0.57">44.2 GB</td></tr><tr title="Nov 9 · 45.5 GB"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 9</span></th><td data-v="0.62">45.5 GB</td></tr><tr title="Nov 10 · 47.5 GB"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 10</span></th><td data-v="0.7">47.5 GB</td></tr><tr title="Nov 11 · 47.0 GB"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 11</span></th><td data-v="0.68">47.0 GB</td></tr><tr title="Nov 12 · 48.5 GB"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 12</span></th><td data-v="0.74">48.5 GB</td></tr><tr title="Nov 13 · 50.0 GB"><th scope="row"><span class="visually-hidden">Nov 13</span></th><td data-v="0.8">50.0 GB</td></tr><tr title="Nov 14 · 49.5 GB"><th scope="row">Nov 14</th><td data-v="0.78">49.5 GB</td></tr></tbody>
</table>
```

## Shares of a whole

`chart-bar` with `chart` draws one row as a single bar across: each segment's `data-v` is its share of the whole, and the legend under it names the series - write the share in the legend's words too. The bar is 12 px thick; `--redz-chart-bar-height` sets another.

```html
<table class="chart chart-bar">
	<caption>Payments in November</caption>
	<thead><tr><th scope="col">Method</th><th scope="col">Card, 58%</th><th scope="col">PromptPay, 31%</th><th scope="col">Cash, 11%</th></tr></thead>
	<tbody>
		<tr><th scope="row">November</th><td data-v="0.58">58%</td><td data-v="0.31">31%</td><td data-v="0.11">11%</td></tr>
	</tbody>
</table>
```

`table class="chart-rows"` breaks a whole into rows, longest first: each `tr` a label, its count and its share in words, and a bar under them whose length is the row's `data-v`. The header cells name the columns for a screen reader and are hidden from sight. The bars take the first chart color; a row's `data-tone` gives it a state's.

```html
<table class="chart-rows">
	<caption>Where bookings came from</caption>
	<thead><tr><th scope="col">Source</th><th scope="col">Bookings</th><th scope="col">Share</th></tr></thead>
	<tbody>
		<tr data-v="0.52"><th scope="row">Search</th><td>182</td><td>52%</td></tr>
		<tr data-v="0.27"><th scope="row">Partners</th><td>94</td><td>27%</td></tr>
		<tr data-v="0.14"><th scope="row">Social networks</th><td>49</td><td>14%</td></tr>
		<tr data-v="0.07" data-tone="secondary"><th scope="row">Other</th><td>25</td><td>7%</td></tr>
	</tbody>
</table>
```

## Sparklines

`span class="spark"` with `role="img"` and its summary in `aria-label` draws one bar per run, oldest first: `data-v` its share of the longest, `data-state` - `ok`, `running`, `timeout`, `failed` - its color, `title` its tooltip. 18 px high in a row, `spark-md` 34 px, `spark-lg` 64 px; `spark-median` with `data-median` draws the median as a dashed line.

```html
<table class="table" aria-label="Agents">
	<thead><tr><th scope="col">Agent</th><th scope="col">Last 20 runs</th></tr></thead>
	<tbody>
		<tr><td class="font-monospace">backup.nightly</td><td><span class="spark" role="img" aria-label="20 runs: 18 OK, 1 timeout, 1 failed"><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.31" title="OK · 1.2 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.28" title="OK · 1.1 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.36" title="OK · 1.4 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.33" title="OK · 1.3 s"></i><i data-state="timeout" data-v="1" title="Timeout · 3.9 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.31" title="OK · 1.2 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.26" title="OK · 1 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.38" title="OK · 1.5 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.31" title="OK · 1.2 s"></i><i data-state="failed" data-v="0.72" title="Failed · 2.8 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.33" title="OK · 1.3 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.28" title="OK · 1.1 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.31" title="OK · 1.2 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.41" title="OK · 1.6 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.31" title="OK · 1.2 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.33" title="OK · 1.3 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.28" title="OK · 1.1 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.36" title="OK · 1.4 s"></i><i data-state="ok" data-v="0.31" title="OK · 1.2 s"></i><i data-state="running" data-v="0.15" title="Running · 0.6 s"></i></span></td></tr>
	</tbody>
</table>
```

`spark-line` draws the runs as one line instead of bars - a size over the days, which climbs and falls, not runs that pass or fail -, its `data-v` the share of the scale the page chose.

```html
<p class="hstack gap-8"><span class="font-monospace">files-01</span><span class="spark spark-line" role="img" aria-label="Storage over 10 days: 41 to 48 GB"><i data-v="0.1"></i><i data-v="0.2"></i><i data-v="0.15"></i><i data-v="0.4"></i><i data-v="0.45"></i><i data-v="0.42"></i><i data-v="0.6"></i><i data-v="0.7"></i><i data-v="0.65"></i><i data-v="0.9"></i></span><span class="tabular-nums">48 GB</span></p>
```

### A strip of days

`spark spark-strip` fills its box with one cell a day, oldest first, each its state's colour by `data-tone` - `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `info` -, a day without one a grey track: not a short bar, which would read as a small value. In a `strip`, a box the strip measures, it shows 90 days, 60 below 560 px and 30 below 360 px, the oldest going first; the `strip-head`'s caption with the `data-days` of the days shown is the one that shows, so its words always match. A cell's `title` is its tooltip.

```html
<div class="strip" aria-label="Uptime of the site" role="group">
	<div class="strip-head"><span data-days="90">90 days ago</span><span data-days="60">60 days ago</span><span data-days="30">30 days ago</span><span>Today</span></div>
	<span class="spark spark-strip" role="img" aria-label="90 days: 84 up, 2 slow, 2 down, 2 without data" id="chart-strip-days"></span>
</div>
```

## A board of lanes

`table class="lanes"` lays a time window across: a header cell `lanes-scale` holds the captions, each at its `data-at`, and each row is a lane - its name in the `th`, which may hold a link or a button that shrinks to it and ends in an ellipsis - give it the whole name as its `title` -, and its track in the `td`. In a track `lanes-tick` marks a run at `data-at`, `lanes-tick-once` a single one, and `lanes-span` from `data-from` to `data-to` a run that goes on, hatched, with its caption. The red line is now, at the table's `data-now` - 0, the start, by default; the grid has `--redz-lanes-steps` parts, 8. A caption that would touch the one before it hides, in any language and at any width. Elements that share a [`data-highlight`](table.md#table-highlight) key light together: a lane, its track included, and its row in a table.

```html
<table class="lanes">
	<caption>The next 24 hours</caption>
	<thead><tr><td></td><th class="lanes-scale" scope="col"><span data-at="0">now</span><span data-at="0.125">18:00</span><span data-at="0.25">21:00</span><span data-at="0.375">00:00</span><span data-at="0.5">03:00</span><span data-at="0.625">06:00</span><span data-at="0.75">09:00</span><span data-at="0.875">12:00</span><span data-at="1">15:00</span></th></tr></thead>
	<tbody>
		<tr data-highlight="mail.queue"><th scope="row">mail.queue</th><td><span class="lanes-span" data-from="0" data-to="1" title="mail.queue - every minute">continuous</span></td></tr>
		<tr data-highlight="backup.nightly"><th scope="row">backup.nightly</th><td><i class="lanes-tick-once lanes-tick" data-at="0.458" title="backup.nightly - 02:00"></i></td></tr>
		<tr data-highlight="fx.rates"><th scope="row">fx.rates</th><td><i class="lanes-tick" data-at="0.04" title="fx.rates - 16:00"></i><i class="lanes-tick" data-at="0.207" title="fx.rates - 20:00"></i><i class="lanes-tick" data-at="0.373" title="fx.rates - 00:00"></i><i class="lanes-tick" data-at="0.54" title="fx.rates - 04:00"></i><i class="lanes-tick" data-at="0.707" title="fx.rates - 08:00"></i><i class="lanes-tick" data-at="0.873" title="fx.rates - 12:00"></i></td></tr>
		<tr data-highlight="invoices.send-reminders"><th scope="row"><button class="btn btn-text btn-xs" type="button" title="invoices.send-reminders">invoices.send-reminders</button></th><td><i class="lanes-tick" data-at="0.667" title="invoices.send-reminders - 07:00"></i></td></tr>
	</tbody>
</table>
<table class="table" aria-label="Agents">
	<thead><tr><th scope="col">Agent</th><th scope="col">Next run</th></tr></thead>
	<tbody>
		<tr data-highlight="mail.queue"><td class="font-monospace">mail.queue</td><td>Every minute</td></tr>
		<tr data-highlight="backup.nightly"><td class="font-monospace">backup.nightly</td><td>02:00</td></tr>
		<tr data-highlight="fx.rates"><td class="font-monospace">fx.rates</td><td>16:00</td></tr>
		<tr data-highlight="invoices.send-reminders"><td class="font-monospace">invoices.send-reminders</td><td>07:00</td></tr>
	</tbody>
</table>
```

## Accessibility

- A chart is its table: the caption names it, the header cells name the series, each row says its day and its numbers. `charts.js` gives a `chart` or `chart-rows` table the table's roles, since WebKit drops them once CSS lays the table out otherwise.
- A share bar and breakdown rows say their shares in words - the legend's, the rows' - and the bar repeats them.
- A color never speaks alone: the legend names every series, a state's segment is named by its header cell, and a sparkline's summary is its name.
- Three of the light theme's series colors are under 3:1 against the page: the legend and the table are what tell them apart.
- In forced colors every bar is drawn in the text color; the numbers are in the table.
